title: Indra goes back four times
hookLine: Indra studies with Prajapati for a hundred and one years, and goes back four times, before he learns what the self is
carry: om: waking, dream, deep sleep, and the self beneath
last: JIVANMUKTI: THE KING WHO STAYED KING.

lines: A SELF BEYOND DEATH AND GRIEF.
A REFLECTION. A DREAMER. A SLEEPER.
cards: In the Chandogya Upanishad, the creator Prajapati announces: there is a self free from old age, death, grief, hunger and thirst. Find it, and you gain every world.

Indra, king of the gods, and Virochana, king of the demons, both come to learn, fuel in hand, as students do. After thirty-two years, Prajapati has them look at themselves, dressed in their finest, in a pan of water.
Virochana leaves satisfied: the body is the self. Indra, on the road, worries: if the body is blind, is the self blind? Back he goes.
Thirty-two more years: the self is the one who roams in dreams. But dreamers weep and are chased. Back again: the self is the one in dreamless sleep.

teach.b: Indra climbed through three answers, body, dreamer, deep sleeper, before the fourth. A very short Upanishad, the Mandukya, first met back in year one, maps the same ground, and many teachers read the two side by side.
It opens: all this is Om. The self has four quarters. Waking, turned outward to a world of solid things.
Dreaming, turned inward to a world made of mind. Deep sleep, where nothing is wanted and no dream is seen, full of ease.
And turiya, the fourth, described by what it is not: not inward, not outward, not knowing, not unknowing. Peaceful, not two. That is the self.

teach.h: WAKING, DREAM, SLEEP, AND THE FOURTH.
teach.b: Then it lays Om over the map: A is waking, U is dreaming, M is deep sleep, and the fourth has no letter; some readers hear it in the silence after.

teach.h: A, U, M, AND THE SILENCE.
teach.b: Gaudapada's karika, verses tradition credits to the teacher of Shankara's teacher, says the one self is known as three in the three states.
Teachers give this as one reason Om opens and closes so much Hindu prayer: its sounds hold every state a person passes through, and its silence points to the self beneath them.

how: In Advaita Vedanta the Mandukya Upanishad is traditionally studied together with Gaudapada's karika and Shankara's commentary, and Om is often chanted at the start and end of Hindu prayer and study.

games.q: the Mandukya's map — tap the pairs.
p: deep sleep, no dream, no wanting

s: Virochana went back to Prajapati as many times as Indra
Virochana left after the first answer, sure the body was the self. only Indra kept going back.
the Upanishad names it by its place, and describes it mostly by what it is not.
the Mandukya gives the fourth state its own letter
A, U and M are the three states. the fourth has no letter; some readers hear it in the silence.

games.q: Prajapati says the self is the one in dreamless sleep. you're Indra. what do you do?
o: accept it and go home: deep sleep is peaceful enough.
go back: in deep sleep he knows nothing, not even himself.
decide the body was the self after all.
games.why: Indra went back a fourth time and learned of the deathless self beneath all three. the Mandukya calls it turiya, the fourth.

practice: If you like, say Om once, softly or silently, and let the sound fade on its own; then rest in the quiet that follows, without filling it. When the mind starts talking, say Om again and rest once more in the quiet after it.
If saying Om isn't part of your life, just listen to the room, and to the quiet between sounds; if you pray, let the silence be your prayer.

wordCard.voice: The Mandukya Karika. Verses, tradition says by Gaudapada, on the Mandukya Upanishad: Om, the three states of waking, dream and deep sleep, and the fourth.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the fourth; the Mandukya's name for the self beyond waking, dream and deep sleep.

carryVoice: Your line: om: waking, dream, deep sleep, and the self beneath. Indra went back four times. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Chandogya Upanishad 8.7–8.12 (Prajapati's self free from old age, death and grief; Indra and Virochana come fuel in hand; the reflection in a pan of water; Virochana leaves; Indra returns for the dream self, the deep-sleep self, and finally the deathless, bodiless self; 101 years in all)
Mandukya Upanishad 1–12 (all this is Om; the four quarters of the self; A, U, M as waking, dream, deep sleep; the fourth without parts)
Gaudapada, Mandukya Karika 1.1–1.5 and 1.16 (the one self known as three in the three states; when the one asleep in beginningless maya awakes, the unborn, sleepless, dreamless non-dual is known)
